hero.title: Don't burn your stubble. Sell it.
hero.problem: Paddy stubble is burned every October and November, wheat stubble every April and May. The smoke spreads across north India.
hero.offer: Parali Setu connects you with biomass plants, mills and feed makers who pay for it and pick it up.
hero.transporter: Have a tractor-trolley or truck? Join as a transporter
hero.artLabel: A harvested field with round stubble bales under the sun

impact.title: Stubble that was not burnt
impact.sub: Live totals from every delivery made through Parali Setu.
impact.tonnesUnit: tonnes kept out of the fire

farmer.title: List your stubble
farmer.body: Add your crop, the rough quantity and your village. An admin checks it before it goes live.

buyer.title: Offer and agree a price
buyer.body: Buyers send an offer per tonne. The farmer accepts it, rejects it or sends back one counter price.

transporter.title: Pick up and deliver
transporter.body: A nearby transporter collects the bales from the field. The farmer is paid once the buyer receives them.

price.title: A fair price, worked out in the open
price.body: We suggest a price band for every listing so farmers are not underpaid and buyers are not overcharged.
price.regionBody: Stubble prices differ between districts of Punjab and Haryana.
price.distanceBody: Farms close to plants and good roads get a better rate. Remote farms still get a fair floor.
price.deliveredBody: Buyers see one price per tonne that already includes pickup and transport. No hidden extras.

buyers.title: Who buys stubble
buyers.body: Power plants burn it for electricity, mills press it into board and paper, dairies feed it to cattle and mushroom farms grow on it.

final.title: This season, let the stubble earn instead of burn.
final.body: Signing up is free. Choose how you want to take part.

manifesto.text: Burning one tonne of paddy or wheat straw puts about 1.4 tonnes of CO₂ and 8 kg of fine smoke into the air. Sold here, that tonne goes to a power plant or a mill instead.

bigger.title: Punjab and Haryana still burn millions of tonnes of straw every year. That straw has buyers.
bigger.sub: Paddy straw is burned in October and November, wheat straw in April and May. Fire counts have fallen since 2023, but satellites still map about 30,000 km² of burned paddy fields.

bigger.fixTitle: How burning is stopped, and where we fit

seeder.title: Sow through it
seeder.body: A Happy Seeder or Super Seeder sows wheat straight into the paddy straw, so nothing is left to burn.

rot.title: Let it rot
rot.body: A spray such as the PUSA bio-decomposer breaks stubble down in the field over a few weeks.

sell.title: Sell it
sell.body: Balers pack straw for power plants, bio-CNG plants, boilers, pellet makers and paper mills. Punjab sent about 70 lakh tonnes this way in 2025.

feed.title: Feed and grow
feed.body: Wheat straw is already cattle fodder (bhusa). Paddy straw can grow mushrooms.

govt.title: Government help
govt.body: 50–80% subsidy on residue machines, ₹1,200 an acre in Haryana for not burning, and pellet rules for power plants and brick kilns.

setu.title: Where Parali Setu fits
setu.body: The machines and the buyers exist. We link a farmer with straw, a transporter and a plant that needs it, before the field has to be cleared.

bigger.method: Burned tonnes: about 28,800 km² of burned fields × 5 tonnes of straw a hectare × half actually burned. CO₂ 1.43 tonnes and PM2.5 8.2 kg per tonne burned. Bales at 140 kg per m³, 2,500 m³ to a pool. Price ₹1,500 a tonne, 2.5 tonnes an acre. Official Punjab figures say almost all straw is now managed; the satellite data disagrees.
